chunks: Resistor symbol (US vs IEC). The question: Draw the symbol for a resistor.
A schematic symbol is a quick drawing that stands for a real part. The resistor has two common styles.
In US-style drawings it is a zigzag line, and in IEC (international, common in Europe) drawings it is a plain rectangle. They mean exactly the same thing.
A resistor has no polarity, so it works the same either way around.
Think of road signs, which look a little different from country to country but carry the same message. The zigzag and the rectangle are two dialects for one idea.
Small changes to the picture, like an arrow added through or into the body, tell you the resistor is a special type.
The analogy is loose, since the symbol also carries labels like R1 and 10 k that make it unambiguous.
Same part, two drawing conventions. Neither has polarity, so you can rotate or mirror it freely. CAD libraries let you choose which one the schematic uses.
Schematic symbol: the standard drawing used in place of a real part. Reference designator: the label like R1 or R2 that names one specific part.
Polarity: having a required direction, like a battery. Resistors have none. Potentiometer: a variable resistor with three terminals, including a movable wiper.
Thermistor: a resistor whose value changes with temperature.
Draw a short zigzag with a wire at each end. Write R1 next to it and 10 k beneath it. That is a complete resistor on a schematic.
If you flip it around, nothing changes, because it has no polarity. Now add an arrow pointing at the middle of the zigzag. It becomes a potentiometer with three terminals.
"A resistor is a zigzag line in US-style schematics, or a plain rectangle in IEC drawings. It's a two-terminal part with no polarity.
I label it with a reference designator like R1 and a value like 10 k. A potentiometer adds an arrow to the middle for the wiper, giving three terminals.
A thermistor adds a diagonal line and a little t. I'd also mark junction dots so the connections are clear."
Quick check. Which statement is true about a fixed resistor's schematic symbol?
